summary: The cut strip is mostly clean, with one stiff T-pose at the start. The second strip has a washed-out, low-contrast look at 123.93 that clears by 124.16, and a small camera or pose jump at 124.03 to 124.06.

faults.what: The frame is washed out and low-contrast, like a ghosted dissolve or exposure lift. Contrast and saturation then build over about 8 frames until 124.16. This matches the measured spike and reads as a flash or fade rather than a deliberate look.
faults.fix: Remove the stray fade or exposure ramp at 123.9 to 124.1, or make it a deliberate quick hit.

faults.what: Between 124.03 and 124.06 the background shifts (gift boxes and turkeys move). The head and torso also change position and scale and the raised hand drops, with no in-between. It reads as a camera or framing hop rather than a smooth push-in.
faults.fix: Smooth the camera push-in keys around 124.0 to 124.06, and check the pose blend at that point.

faults.what: On the first frames of the shot both arms are held out in a stiff, symmetrical T-shape with limp, dangling hands. The line of action is weak. The arms then fold down quickly with no anticipation.
faults.fix: Start on a clearer asymmetric pose, or add a small anticipation before the arm drop.
